meta.description: Curated 15-question multi-hop eval set adapted from HotpotQA bridge/comparison types. Documents are embedded as wiki pages for end-to-end testing of cross-page retrieval. No network dependency — runs fully deterministic.
meta.source: HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018) — hand-picked bridge and comparison questions

questions.question: Which magazine was started first, Arthur's Magazine or First for Women?
questions.expected_answer: Arthur's Magazine was started first (1844 vs 1989).

questions.question: Were Scott Derrickson and Ed Wood of the same nationality?
questions.expected_answer: No. Scott Derrickson is American and Ed Wood was also American, so they were of the same nationality.

questions.question: The director of the romantic comedy 'Big Stone Gap' is based in what New York city?
questions.expected_answer: The director Adriana Trigiani is based in New York City.

questions.question: What government position was held by the woman who portrayed Corliss Archer in the film 'Kiss and Tell'?
questions.expected_answer: Shirley Temple, who portrayed Corliss Archer, later served as U.S. Ambassador to Ghana and Czechoslovakia, and Chief of Protocol of the United States.

questions.question: The singer who wrote the song 'Grandma's Hands' also acted in which John Singleton film?
questions.expected_answer: Bill Withers acted in the film 'Baby Boy' directed by John Singleton.

questions.question: Who is older, Danny Glover or Mel Gibson?
questions.expected_answer: Danny Glover is older. He was born in 1946, while Mel Gibson was born in 1956.

questions.question: Which film has a longer runtime, 'The Dark Knight' or 'Inception'?
questions.expected_answer: The Dark Knight has a longer runtime at 152 minutes versus Inception's 148 minutes.

questions.question: What year was the father of Malcolm X born?
questions.expected_answer: Earl Little, the father of Malcolm X, was born in 1890.

questions.question: The author of the novel 'The Water Dancer' teaches at which university?
questions.expected_answer: Ta-Nehisi Coates teaches at New York University (NYU).

questions.question: What is the capital of the country where the city of Gonder is located?
questions.expected_answer: Gonder is located in Ethiopia, whose capital is Addis Ababa.

questions.question: Who was the lead actor in the film that won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 1994?
questions.expected_answer: Tom Hanks was the lead actor in 'Forrest Gump', which won Best Picture in 1994.

questions.question: Which team does the player who scored the most goals in the 2014 FIFA World Cup play for at club level?
questions.expected_answer: James Rodríguez, the top scorer of the 2014 World Cup, played for Real Madrid at club level during that time.

questions.question: Which city has a larger population, Tokyo or Delhi?
questions.expected_answer: Tokyo has a larger population than Delhi. Tokyo metropolitan area has approximately 37 million, while Delhi has approximately 32 million.

questions.question: What record label was the album 'Random Access Memories' released under?
questions.expected_answer: Random Access Memories was released under Columbia Records.

questions.question: In which century did the composer of the opera 'The Marriage of Figaro' live?
questions.expected_answer: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, the composer of The Marriage of Figaro, lived in the 18th century (1756-1791).

_wiki_documents._description: Wikipedia-style context paragraphs for each supporting document. These are ingested as wiki pages before running eval.

Arthur's Magazine.content:
# Arthur's Magazine

Arthur's Magazine (1844–1846) was an American literary periodical published in Philadelphia in the 19th century. Edited by Timothy Shay Arthur, it featured mostly domestic fiction and writings on moral reform. The magazine lasted only about two years, with the first issue appearing in 1844. It was known for publishing works by Edgar Allan Poe and other notable authors of the period. Arthur later became famous for his temperance novel 'Ten Nights in a Bar-Room'.

## Key Facts
- First published: 1844
- Last published: 1846
- Location: Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
- Genre: Literary periodical, domestic fiction

First for Women.content:
# First for Women

First for Women is an American women's magazine published by Bauer Media Group. It was launched in 1989 and focuses on health, wellness, diet, nutrition, fashion, and beauty topics. The magazine is known for featuring celebrity cover stories and practical lifestyle advice. It is published on a monthly basis and has a circulation of approximately 4 million readers. The target demographic is women aged 35-55.

## Key Facts
- First published: 1989
- Publisher: Bauer Media Group
- Frequency: Monthly
- Category: Women's lifestyle magazine

Scott Derrickson.content:
# Scott Derrickson

Scott Derrickson (born July 16, 1966) is an American filmmaker, director, and screenwriter. He is best known for directing horror films such as 'The Exorcism of Emily Rose' (2005), 'Sinister' (2012), and 'Deliver Us from Evil' (2014), as well as the Marvel Cinematic Universe superhero film 'Doctor Strange' (2016). Derrickson was born in Denver, Colorado and graduated from Biola University and the USC School of Cinematic Arts.

## Key Facts
- Nationality: American
- Born: July 16, 1966
- Birthplace: Denver, Colorado, United States
- Notable works: Doctor Strange, Sinister, The Exorcism of Emily Rose

Ed Wood.content:
# Ed Wood

Edward Davis Wood Jr. (October 10, 1924 – December 10, 1978) was an American filmmaker, actor, and author. He is widely regarded as one of the worst directors in cinema history, known for low-budget science fiction and horror films such as 'Plan 9 from Outer Space' (1957), which has been called the worst film ever made. His life was portrayed by Johnny Depp in Tim Burton's 1994 biopic 'Ed Wood'.

## Key Facts
- Nationality: American
- Born: October 10, 1924
- Birthplace: Poughkeepsie, New York, United States
- Died: December 10, 1978
- Notable for: Plan 9 from Outer Space

Big Stone Gap (film).content:
# Big Stone Gap (film)

Big Stone Gap is a 2014 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Adriana Trigiani, based on her 2000 novel of the same name. The film stars Ashley Judd, Patrick Wilson, Whoopi Goldberg, and Jane Krakowski. Set in the Appalachian town of Big Stone Gap, Virginia, the story follows a spinsterish pharmacist who discovers a long-hidden secret. The film premiered at the Virginia Film Festival on November 7, 2014.

## Key Facts
- Director: Adriana Trigiani
- Release year: 2014
- Genre: Romantic comedy
- Based on: Big Stone Gap novel (2000) by Adriana Trigiani

Adriana Trigiani.content:
# Adriana Trigiani

Adriana Trigiani is an American author, television writer, film director, and entrepreneur based in New York City. She is best known for her Big Stone Gap series of novels. Trigiani has written over 18 books and her works have been published in 38 countries. She also wrote and directed the film adaptation of her novel 'Big Stone Gap'. She co-founded the all-female comedy troupe 'The Outcasts' and has written for several television shows.

## Key Facts
- Location: New York City, New York
- Nationality: American
- Notable works: Big Stone Gap series, The Shoemaker's Wife
- Occupation: Author, film director, television writer

Kiss and Tell (1945 film).content:
# Kiss and Tell (1945 film)

Kiss and Tell is a 1945 American comedy film directed by Richard Wallace and starring Shirley Temple, Jerome Courtland, and Walter Abel. The film is based on the 1943 play of the same name by F. Hugh Herbert. In the film, Shirley Temple portrays the character Corliss Archer, a teenage girl whose innocent actions cause chaos and misunderstandings among her family and friends during wartime.

## Key Facts
- Release year: 1945
- Director: Richard Wallace
- Starring: Shirley Temple (as Corliss Archer)
- Genre: Comedy
- Based on: Kiss and Tell play (1943)

Shirley Temple.content:
# Shirley Temple

Shirley Temple Black (April 23, 1928 – February 10, 2014) was an American actress, singer, dancer, and diplomat. As a child star, she was Hollywood's number-one box-office draw from 1935 to 1938. After her film career, she entered public service, serving as U.S. Ambassador to Ghana (1974–1976) and later as U.S. Ambassador to Czechoslovakia (1989–1992). She also served as Chief of Protocol of the United States (1976–1977).

## Key Facts
- Born: April 23, 1928
- Died: February 10, 2014
- Government positions: U.S. Ambassador to Ghana, U.S. Ambassador to Czechoslovakia, Chief of Protocol
- Notable films: Bright Eyes, The Little Colonel, Heidi

Grandma's Hands (song).content:
# Grandma's Hands (song)

'Grandma's Hands' is a song written and performed by Bill Withers, released on his 1971 debut album 'Just As I Am'. The song is a tribute to Withers' grandmother, Lula Carter, who helped raise him. It has been covered by numerous artists including Barbra Streisand, The Staple Singers, and John Legend. The song was also prominently sampled in the 2002 hit 'No Diggity' by Blackstreet.

## Key Facts
- Artist: Bill Withers
- Album: Just As I Am
- Release year: 1971
- Genre: Soul, R&B

Bill Withers.content:
# Bill Withers

William Harrison Withers Jr. (July 4, 1938 – March 30, 2020) was an American singer-songwriter and musician. He had several major hits including 'Ain't No Sunshine' (1971), 'Lean on Me' (1972), 'Lovely Day' (1977), and 'Just the Two of Us' (1981). Withers also appeared as an actor in the 2001 film 'Baby Boy', directed by John Singleton. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2015.

## Key Facts
- Born: July 4, 1938
- Died: March 30, 2020
- Film appearance: Baby Boy (2001), directed by John Singleton
- Major hits: Ain't No Sunshine, Lean on Me, Lovely Day

Danny Glover.content:
# Danny Glover

Danny Lebern Glover (born July 22, 1946) is an American actor, film director, and political activist. He is best known for his role as Roger Murtaugh in the 'Lethal Weapon' film series. Glover has appeared in many other films including 'The Color Purple' (1985), 'Predator 2' (1990), and 'To Sleep with Anger' (1990). He is also known for his civil rights and political activism, serving as a Goodwill Ambassador for the United Nations Development Programme.

## Key Facts
- Born: July 22, 1946
- Birthplace: San Francisco, California, United States
- Notable roles: Roger Murtaugh (Lethal Weapon series)
- Also known as: Political activist, UN Goodwill Ambassador

Mel Gibson.content:
# Mel Gibson

Mel Columcille Gerard Gibson (born January 3, 1956) is an American actor, film director, and producer. He is best known for his roles in the 'Mad Max' and 'Lethal Weapon' film series, and for directing the Academy Award-winning films 'Braveheart' (1995) and 'Hacksaw Ridge' (2016). Gibson was born in Peekskill, New York, and moved to Australia with his family at age 12.

## Key Facts
- Born: January 3, 1956
- Birthplace: Peekskill, New York, United States
- Notable works: Braveheart, Mad Max, Lethal Weapon series
- Academy Awards: Best Director (Braveheart, 1995)

The Dark Knight (film).content:
# The Dark Knight (film)

The Dark Knight is a 2008 superhero film directed by Christopher Nolan, based on the DC Comics character Batman. The film stars Christian Bale as Batman, with Heath Ledger as the Joker. The film's runtime is 152 minutes (2 hours and 32 minutes). It received critical acclaim, particularly for Ledger's performance, and grossed over $1 billion worldwide. Ledger posthumously won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

## Key Facts
- Director: Christopher Nolan
- Release year: 2008
- Runtime: 152 minutes
- Starring: Christian Bale, Heath Ledger

Inception.content:
# Inception

Inception is a 2010 science fiction action film written and directed by Christopher Nolan. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio as a professional thief who steals information by entering the subconscious of his targets. The runtime is 148 minutes (2 hours and 28 minutes). It won four Academy Awards including Best Cinematography, and was nominated for Best Picture. The film grossed over $836 million worldwide.

## Key Facts
- Director: Christopher Nolan
- Release year: 2010
- Runtime: 148 minutes
- Starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page

Malcolm X.content:
# Malcolm X

Malcolm X (born Malcolm Little; May 19, 1925 – February 21, 1965) was an African-American Muslim minister and human rights activist. He was a prominent figure during the civil rights movement and a vocal advocate for Black empowerment. His father, Earl Little, was a Baptist minister and an organizer for the Universal Negro Improvement Association. Malcolm X was assassinated in 1965 while giving a speech in New York City.

## Key Facts
- Born: May 19, 1925
- Father: Earl Little
- Died: February 21, 1965
- Known for: Civil rights activism, Black empowerment advocacy

Earl Little.content:
# Earl Little

Earl Little (1890 – September 28, 1931) was an African-American Baptist minister and activist. He was the father of Malcolm X and an organizer for the Universal Negro Improvement Association (UNIA), which was founded by Marcus Garvey. Earl Little was born in Reynolds, Georgia in 1890. He died under suspicious circumstances in 1931 in Lansing, Michigan, when Malcolm was six years old.

## Key Facts
- Born: 1890
- Birthplace: Reynolds, Georgia, United States
- Died: September 28, 1931
- Occupation: Baptist minister, UNIA organizer
- Notable for: Father of Malcolm X

The Water Dancer.content:
# The Water Dancer

The Water Dancer is the debut novel by Ta-Nehisi Coates, published on September 24, 2019, by One World (an imprint of Random House). The novel is a work of historical fiction set in the antebellum South. It follows the story of Hiram Walker, a young enslaved man who possesses a mysterious power called 'Conduction' that allows him to transport himself and others across space. Oprah Winfrey selected it for her book club.

## Key Facts
- Author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
- Published: September 24, 2019
- Genre: Historical fiction, magical realism
- Publisher: One World (Random House)

Ta-Nehisi Coates.content:
# Ta-Nehisi Coates

Ta-Nehisi Paul Coates (born September 30, 1975) is an American author, journalist, and educator. He gained prominence as a national correspondent for The Atlantic, where he wrote about cultural, social, and political issues. His book 'Between the World and Me' won the 2015 National Book Award for Nonfiction. Coates teaches at New York University (NYU) where he is a distinguished writer in residence at the Arthur L. Carter Journalism Institute.

## Key Facts
- Born: September 30, 1975
- Institution: New York University (NYU)
- Position: Distinguished Writer in Residence
- Notable works: Between the World and Me, The Water Dancer

Gonder.content:
# Gonder

Gonder (also spelled Gondar) is a city and separate woreda in Ethiopia. Located in the Semien Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region, Gonder is north of Lake Tana on the Lesser Angereb River and southwest of the Simien Mountains. It was the capital of the Ethiopian Empire under Emperor Fasilides in the 17th century and is known for its historic castles and palaces. The city has a population of approximately 300,000.

## Key Facts
- Country: Ethiopia
- Region: Amhara Region
- Known for: Historic castles, Fasil Ghebbi (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
- Historical significance: Capital of Ethiopian Empire in 17th century

Ethiopia.content:
# Ethiopia

Ethiopia, officially the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa. It is the second-most populous country in Africa, with over 120 million people. The capital and largest city is Addis Ababa. Ethiopia has a rich history as one of the oldest nations in the world, being the only African country that was never colonized (with the exception of a five-year Italian occupation).

## Key Facts
- Capital: Addis Ababa
- Population: Over 120 million
- Region: Horn of Africa
- Official languages: Amharic, Oromo, Somali, Tigrinya
- Notable: Never colonized (except brief Italian occupation)

Forrest Gump.content:
# Forrest Gump

Forrest Gump is a 1994 American comedy-drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis and written by Eric Roth. The film stars Tom Hanks as the title character, a slow-witted but kind-hearted man from Alabama who witnesses and influences several defining historical events in the 20th century. It won the Academy Award for Best Picture at the 67th Academy Awards, along with five other Oscars including Best Director and Best Actor for Hanks.

## Key Facts
- Director: Robert Zemeckis
- Starring: Tom Hanks (lead actor)
- Academy Award: Best Picture (1994)
- Release year: 1994
- Other Oscars: Best Director, Best Actor (Tom Hanks), Best Adapted Screenplay

Academy Award for Best Picture.content:
# Academy Award for Best Picture

The Academy Award for Best Picture is one of the Academy Awards presented annually by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS) since the awards debuted in 1929. This award goes to the producers of the film and is the only category in which every member of the Academy is eligible to submit a nomination and vote on the final ballot. The 1994 winner was 'Forrest Gump', directed by Robert Zemeckis and starring Tom Hanks. Other notable winners include 'Titanic' (1997), 'The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King' (2003), and 'Parasite' (2019).

## Key Facts
- First awarded: 1929
- 1994 winner: Forrest Gump
- Presented by: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS)
- Voted by: All Academy members

2014 FIFA World Cup.content:
# 2014 FIFA World Cup

The 2014 FIFA World Cup was the 20th FIFA World Cup, held in Brazil from June 12 to July 13, 2014. Germany won the tournament, defeating Argentina 1–0 in the final. The top scorer (Golden Boot winner) of the tournament was James Rodríguez of Colombia, who scored six goals. Rodríguez's performances earned him a transfer from AS Monaco to Real Madrid later that summer.

## Key Facts
- Host country: Brazil
- Winner: Germany
- Top scorer: James Rodríguez (Colombia) — 6 goals
- Dates: June 12 – July 13, 2014

James Rodríguez.content:
# James Rodríguez

James David Rodríguez Rubio (born July 12, 1991) is a Colombian professional footballer. He rose to global prominence at the 2014 FIFA World Cup in Brazil, where he won the Golden Boot as the tournament's top scorer with six goals. Following his World Cup performance, he transferred from AS Monaco to Real Madrid in July 2014 for a reported fee of €80 million. He has also played for Bayern Munich (on loan), Everton, Al-Rayyan, and São Paulo.

## Key Facts
- Born: July 12, 1991
- Nationality: Colombian
- 2014 World Cup: Golden Boot winner (6 goals)
- Club during 2014-2017: Real Madrid
- Transfer fee (2014): €80 million (Monaco → Real Madrid)

Tokyo.content:
# Tokyo

Tokyo, officially the Tokyo Metropolis, is the capital and most populous city of Japan. The Greater Tokyo Area is the most populous metropolitan area in the world, with a population of approximately 37.4 million residents as of 2024. Tokyo is a major global financial center and is known for its blend of ultramodern and traditional architecture, from neon-lit skyscrapers to historic temples.

## Key Facts
- Country: Japan
- Population (metro): Approximately 37.4 million
- Status: Capital of Japan
- Known for: World's most populous metropolitan area, global financial center

Delhi.content:
# Delhi

Delhi, officially the National Capital Territory of Delhi (NCT), is a city and a union territory of India. It is the capital of India and part of the National Capital Region (NCR). The population of Delhi is approximately 32 million in the extended urban area (National Capital Region). Delhi is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, with a history spanning several millennia.

## Key Facts
- Country: India
- Population (NCR): Approximately 32 million
- Status: Capital of India
- Known for: Rich history, Red Fort, India Gate

Random Access Memories.content:
# Random Access Memories

Random Access Memories is the fourth and final studio album by French electronic music duo Daft Punk, released on May 17, 2013, by Columbia Records. The album features collaborations with various artists including Pharrell Williams, Nile Rodgers, and Giorgio Moroder. It won Album of the Year at the 56th Annual Grammy Awards, among other accolades. The lead single 'Get Lucky' became a worldwide hit.

## Key Facts
- Artist: Daft Punk
- Release date: May 17, 2013
- Record label: Columbia Records
- Grammy: Album of the Year (2014)
- Hit single: Get Lucky (feat. Pharrell Williams)

Daft Punk.content:
# Daft Punk

Daft Punk was a French electronic music duo formed in 1993 by Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo and Thomas Bangalter. They are widely regarded as one of the most influential acts in electronic music history. Their final studio album, 'Random Access Memories', was released in 2013 by Columbia Records and won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year. The duo announced their split in February 2021 after 28 years together.

## Key Facts
- Formed: 1993
- Disbanded: 2021
- Members: Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, Thomas Bangalter
- Record label: Columbia Records (Random Access Memories era)
- Notable albums: Homework, Discovery, Random Access Memories

The Marriage of Figaro.content:
# The Marriage of Figaro

The Marriage of Figaro (Italian: Le nozze di Figaro), K. 492, is an opera buffa (comic opera) in four acts composed in 1786 by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, with an Italian libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte. It is based on the 1784 stage comedy by Pierre Beaumarchais. The opera is considered one of the greatest operas ever written and is a staple of the standard operatic repertoire worldwide.

## Key Facts
- Composer: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
- Year composed: 1786
- Language: Italian
- Genre: Opera buffa (comic opera)
- Librettist: Lorenzo Da Ponte

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.content:
# Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (27 January 1756 – 5 December 1791) was a prolific and influential composer of the Classical period. Born in Salzburg, he composed more than 800 works across virtually every genre of his time, including symphonies, concertos, chamber music, operas, and choral music. His opera 'The Marriage of Figaro' premiered in 1786 and remains one of the most frequently performed operas worldwide.

## Key Facts
- Born: January 27, 1756 (18th century)
- Died: December 5, 1791
- Period: Classical
- Notable operas: The Marriage of Figaro, Don Giovanni, The Magic Flute
- Total works: Over 800 compositions
